I wasn't going to use tools, so I haven't written `tasks.md`. Below is the content, ready to save. Say the word and I'll write it, or paste it in yourself.

The plan doesn't pin down a few things that block implementation: format, what "all data" means, and what "fast" means. I haven't reopened the plan. I turned each gap into a short, time-boxed task with a default, so you can keep moving.

```markdown
# User Data Export: Implementation Tasks

Source plan (approved): Build an API endpoint that exports all of a user's data. Use whatever format is easiest. Should be fast. Ship next week.

## 0. Pin down open points (about 1 hour, before coding)
Defaults below apply unless someone overrides them.
- [ ] 0.1 Format: JSON (easiest, and machine-readable). Single file, UTF-8.
- [ ] 0.2 Scope: list every table/store holding user-owned data. Write the list in this file under "Data sources". Include exclusions and why (e.g., other users' data, internal audit fields).
- [ ] 0.3 "Fast" target: p95 under 2s for a typical user. Anything larger goes async (see 4.x).
- [ ] 0.4 Authorization: a user can export only their own data. Admin export is out of scope.
- [ ] 0.5 Confirm with the PM or legal whether the export has compliance implications (e.g., GDPR/CCPA access requests). If so, scope and format may be constrained.

## 1. Endpoint skeleton
- [ ] 1.1 Add `GET /api/users/me/export` behind existing authentication.
- [ ] 1.2 Return `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=export-<userId>-<date>.json`.
- [ ] 1.3 Define the response schema with a `schemaVersion` field.

## 2. Data collection
- [ ] 2.1 One collector function per data source from 0.2, each returning plain serializable data.
- [ ] 2.2 Aggregate collectors into a single export document.
- [ ] 2.3 Strip secrets: password hashes, tokens, API keys, internal IDs not meant for users.

## 3. Performance
- [ ] 3.1 Query per source by indexed user ID. Check for missing indexes.
- [ ] 3.2 Run collectors concurrently.
- [ ] 3.3 Stream the JSON response instead of building it all in memory.
- [ ] 3.4 Benchmark with a small, median, and very large user. Record results against the 0.3 target.

## 4. Large exports (only if 3.4 misses the target)
- [ ] 4.1 Move to an async job: the endpoint returns a job ID and the user polls for status.
- [ ] 4.2 Store the finished file with expiring, user-scoped download access.

## 5. Safety
- [ ] 5.1 Rate-limit the endpoint (e.g., a few requests per user per hour).
- [ ] 5.2 Audit-log each export (user, time, outcome).
- [ ] 5.3 Authorization tests: unauthenticated gets 401, and one user can never receive another user's data.

## 6. Testing
- [ ] 6.1 Unit tests per collector.
- [ ] 6.2 Integration test: a seeded user's export contains every source from 0.2 and none of the stripped fields.
- [ ] 6.3 Test the empty-user and large-user cases.

## 7. Release
- [ ] 7.1 Document the endpoint and the export schema in the API docs.
- [ ] 7.2 Ship behind a feature flag, enable for internal users, then roll out to everyone.
- [ ] 7.3 Add monitoring for latency and error rate.

## Data sources
(Fill in during 0.2.)
```

Tasks 0.2 and 0.5 are the likeliest to cause rework late in the week. If you can get answers on those today, the rest should fit next week's ship date.
